newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices hold amid cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices hold amid cold weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were little changed Thursday as cold weather across the Midwest and Northeast kept most buyers in the market, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast swing gas prices were unchanged in the low-to-mid $1.90s, with Henry Hub quoted mostly at $1.95-1.97 per mmBtu.
Prices on Transco (Station 65) remained strong around $2 due to the hefty heating demand at the New York city-gate, where prices held in the $2.40s.
Appalachian prices drifted a few cents lower to about $2.19 on Columbia and $2.30 on CNG.
Temperatures in the Northeast are not expected to return to near-normal until Wednesday, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Midcontinent, prices were stable in the low-to-mid $1.80s as the post-winter cold air continued to numb the region.
Further west, where temperatures were still more moderate, Permian basin prices failed to budge from about $1.77-1.80.

Southern California border prices fell about three cents to the mid-to-high $1.80s as Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 megawatt Diablo 2 nuclear unit was at 75 percent of capacity this morning and increasing power.
In south Texas, the market clutched onto $1.90 as cooler temperatures in the state kept a lid on demand. Katy prices were mostly in the low-$1.90s.
